name: Colocynthis
author: Dubey
chapter: Dubey Text Book of Materia Medica

sections.title: INTRODUCTION
sections.content: In traditional medicine, Colocynthis has been used as a purgative. But in Hemoeopathy, during proving, the range of action of this medicine made Hahnemann place it high among the remedies for COLIC. Nash says, “No remedy produces more severe coHc than this one and no remedy works more promptly.”

sections.title: CLINICAL
sections.content: Colic, Biliary colic, Diarrhoea, Dysentery, Dysmenorrhoea, Headache, Menstrual, Neuralgia, Rheumatism, Sciatica, Vertigo, etc.

sections.title: SPHERES OF ACTION
sections.content:
It acts on visceral organs, colon rectum and nerves such as abdominal plexus, trigeminal and sciatic nerves.

PATHOGENESIS

It acts upon the colon and rectum to cause colic and evacuation of blood and mucus. It may, even, produce peritonitis. It, acts on the female genital organs’causing ,ovarian neuralgia. Its action on nerves causes neuralgia, sciatica and lumbago.

sections.title: GUIDING SYMPTOMS
sections.content:
1. The strongest characteristic calling for Colocynth is TERRIBLE COLIC WITH AGONISING PAIN in abdomen compelling the patient to bend double. Relief is obtained by MOTION and HARD PRESSURE and the motion is kept up steadily by the patient while the pain lasts. Colic may occur by itself or with dysentery, cholera, etc.

2. Neuralgic affection and rheumatic troubles. Dr. Hughes quotes Dr. Bahr as saying that Colocynth is useful in rheumatic colic and Plumbum in neuralgic colic.

3. Rheumatic pains affecting the joints are much aggravated by motion and better by rest and pressure.

4. Worse from 4.9 p.m., is another characteristic of Colocynth.

5. Shooting pain like lightning shocks down the whole limb, left hip, left thigh, left knee and the popliteal fossa. Crampy pain in the thigh as though screwed in a vice. The patient lies upon the affected side to get relief.

sections.title: PARTICULARS
sections.content:
Headache

Causation: Anger with indignation and mortification, vexation, taking cheese, suppressed menses and exposure to cold.

Location: Headache is normally felt in the frontal region. ;

Character of pain: There is pressive and burning pain in the frontal region with soreness of scalp.

Modalities: Headache is worse by stooping, lying on back, anger and indignation. Better by pressure and by bending head forward.

Concomitants: Confusion and pressive pain in orbit; vertigo on quickly turning the head.

Vertigo

Causation: Anger, indignation, mortification, vexation, suppressed menses and exposure to cold.

Character: There is VERTIGO ON QUICKLY TURNING the HEAD, especially to the left, as if he would fall, with confusion and pressive pain in the orbit. Dullness and giddiness at the beginning of colic. accompained by pressive frontal headache.

Colic

Causation: Anger with indignation, vexation, taking cheese, exposure to cold and suppressed menses

Location: Colicky Pain is felt in the whole abdomen,

Character of pain: There is terrible agonising pain in the abdomen, compelling the patient to bend double, pain is violent and gripping type. Abdomen is very sensitive to touch. Pains come in paroxysms; become very severe every few minutes. The patient twists and turns to get relief.

Modalities: . * Aggravation by eating and drinking, by taking cheese, and by touch.

* Amelioration: By bending double, motion, bending forward, hard pressure and discharge of flatus.

Concomitants: Colicky pain may be attended with neuralgia; headache of violent nature with cutting and boring pain in the head.

author: Dubey
chapter: Dubey Text Book of Materia Medica

sections.title: CLINICAL
sections.content:
Cancer of stomach, Cancer of Breast. Angular stomatitis. Epithelioma of lips or anus. Fissures. Stricture of Oesophagus.

According to the teachings of Hahnemann, Dr. Burnett proved this drug on himself to find out its curative sphere. He regards rhagades at mucocutaneous orifices (Nit. Acid.) and warty excrescences to be most leading indications for it. Dr. Burnett and Dr. Dudgeon both reported a case of cancer of a left breast cured with Condurango, when accompanied by sores or cracks at corners of mouth. Condurango has also cured cancer of the stomach with vomiting of coffee ground masses, loss of appetite, and emaciation. It is also useful in cases of stricture of oesophagus with burning pains behind sternum, where food seems to stick. It stimulates the digestive functions and thus improves the general health.

Author has relieved a case of cancer of left breast in a lady of fifty-nine. Tumour was hard & quiet a big in size and was not improved at all under Hydrastis and Phytolacca. Under Cundurango in tincture doeseit improved miraculously & a lady survived for ten years.

name: Conium Maculatum
author: Dubey
chapter: Dubey Text Book of Materia Medica

sections.title: INTRODUCTION
sections.content:
This is yet another important spinal remedy especially affecting the motor nerves, known as the “Balm of Gilead”. Conium maculatum is the remedy for the diseases of people of climacteric age, especially of women, if the symptoms correspond. What Conium is to the glands and capillary system, Aconite is to the heart and arterial system. In many cases, Conium may be regarded as the “Aconite of chronic diseases.”

The plant contains the active principle, conine, which is very poisonous. It is notorious as an ingredient of the State poison of ancient Greeks, Socrates was killed by Conium. This poisonous property, when potentised, proves to be an excellent remedy, particularly suited to old men, old maids and old bachelors and it was Hahnemann who first showed how the remedy could be utilised safely as well as effectively.

sections.title: CLINICAL
sections.content: Bladder inflammation. Breast affection, Bronchitis, Cancer, Cataract, Chorea, Cough, Eye affection, Glandular affection, Injury, Jaundice, Liver affection, Menstrual disorders, Paralysis, Testicles, Tumours affection of, Ulcers, Vertigo, etc.

sections.title: SPHERES OF ACTION
sections.content:
The seat of action of this remedy is centred on the nervous system, particularly motor nerves first and later on the sensory nerves as well; heart, cardiovascular system, glands and female genital organs.

PATHOGENESIS

It powerfully depresses motor nerves leading to paralysis of the muscles of the body as far as voluntary and reflex motions are concerned. It causes paralysis of the motor nerve filaments of the cerebrospinal system. The sensory nerves, spinal cord and brain are affected later on. It depresses the vagus ganglia, resulting in fall of blood pressure and quick pulse, but lowers the temperature. Its effect on glands causes induration and hypertrophy.

CONSTITUTION

Make-up of the body: It is mostly suited to old men and women, old bachelors, during and after climacteric age. Persons having debility and diseases caused by blow or fall.

The strongest characteristic of Conium maculatum is its peculiar VERTIGO, which is much aggravated by TURNING THE HEAD SIDEWISE or LOOKING AROUND OR TURNING IN BED.

(China, Thuja, Cactus rev. of Sambucus). Very offensive sweat.

. Swelling and induration of glands after contusion or bruise. . Cancerous and scrofulous persons with enlarged glands. . Intermittent flow of urine: great difficulty in passing urine; urine flows, stops and

flows again; from prostatic and uterine affections, or paretic conditions.

. Breast sore, hard and painful, especially during the menstrual period. . Objects look red, rainbow coloured, double vision, weakness of sight, aversion to

light without inflammation, but, with intense photophobia.

_ Desire for warmth especially of the sun, coffee, acid and salty food. . Aversion to open air, light, business, study, bread. Craving for salt, coffee and sour

things. Desire for warmth of sun. Cough when lying down, aggravated from slightest exposure to cold air.

Cold stool and flatulence is a unique characteristic of Coniummac. (Hot stool and flatulence, Sulphur). Ascending type of paralysis reminds of Conium.

Mind : The patient is morose and ill humoured and easily angered. He is very much quarrelsome and scolds always even at silly things.

The patient cannot and will not bear contradiction; excitement of any kind causes mental depression.

The patient has no inclination to business or to study; very much indifferent and indolent; does not take interest in anything.

Very forgetful; weak memory; is uanble to sustain and mental effort. Cannot bear to be alone; dread of being alone; yet avoids society (Kali carb., Lyco.).

Ailments from : Blow or fall, contusion, sexual excess, sexual abstinence or SUPPRESSED SEXUAL DESIRE: suppressed menses, excitement or over work.

sections.title: PARTICULARS
sections.content:
Headache

Causation: Headache is caused by blow or fall, sexual excess, suppressed menses, excitement or over work, insufficient evacuation.

Location: Lancinating pain especially on the vertex and forehead, in temples; semi-lateral.

Sensation: Sensation as if there is much foreign substance in the head. Sensation as if the brain has gone to sleep.

Character of headache: Stupefying pains in the head; excessive sensibility of brain. Tearing and lancinating pain as if the head were beaten to pieces or the contents of skull would be pressed out. Stitching in head while coughing. Headache with numbness of the brain. Attack of tearing headache which compels the patient to lie down. Obstinate shooting pain in the sinciput; heaviness and squeezing sensation. Apoplexy with paralysis of old people.

Modalities

* Aggravation: When walking in the open air; from contact, motion and after eating.

* Amelioration: When lying in a recumbent position or while stooping; by external pressure and © Concomitants: Nausea and vomiting of mucus. Apoplexy with paralysis of old people.

Vertigo : The strongest characteristic of this drug, from the Homoeopathic point of view, IS ITS PECULIAR VERTIGO which aggravated by TURNING THE HEAD SIDEWISE OR TURNING IN THE BED, especially of old people. Feels as if bed were floating. Vertigo after intoxication even after taking a very small quantity. There is whirling Vertigo on rising and sometimes causes a fall, especially in the morning.

Eyes, eye troubles are caused by injury or blow and eye strain; or Using artificial lightly students; sexual excess or suppressed menses and sexual suppression.

Character of eye troubles: There is aversion to light without inflammation of eyes. Ophthalmia with intense photophobia. Weakness and dazzling of the eyes, with giddiness and debility. Weakness of vision. Pupils dilated, the pain is worse at night and terribly aggravated by least ray of light, relieved in a dark room and by pressure.

Gastro-intestinal tract :

Tongue : Tongue is swollen, painful, stiff and paralysed, Consequently, there is difficulty in speech. Bitter taste in the mouth.

Stomach : There is no appetite. Eructations taste sour arid offensive. Terrible nausea with violent vomiting like coffee-ground; acrid heartburn; worse on going to bed. Amelioration from eating, but aggravation a few hours after meals. Cutting pain in the abdomen as from a knife. Severe aching in and around liver. Rumbling with painful tightness of abdomen.

Stool : Cold stool and cold flatulence. Frequent ineffectual urging to stool; passes little at a time. Burning in rectum during stool. Stool is full of undigested matter and painless; passes involuntarily during sleep.

Urine : There is great difficulty in voiding urine; FLOW INTERMITS, STOPS AND THEN FLOWS

AGAIN. Flow stops on straining, from enlarged prostate, uterine affections or paretic conditions. Pain when urinating. Urine is pale with grey or white sediment.

Conium maculatum is the remedy for the diseases of people of climacteric age, especially of women, if the symptoms correspond. What Conium is to the glands and capillary system, Aconite is to the heart and arterial system. In many cases, Conium may be regarded as the “Aconite of chronic diseases.”

The plant contains the active principle, conine, which is very poisonous. It is notorious as an ingredient of the State poison of ancient Greeks, Socrates was killed by Conium. This poisonous property, when potentised, proves to be an excellent remedy, particularly suited to old men, old maids and old bachelors and it was Hahnemann who first showed how the remedy could be utilised safely as well as effectively.
CLINICAL: Bladder inflammation. Breast affection, Bronchitis, Cancer, Cataract, Chorea, Cough, Eye affection, Glandular affection, Injury, Jaundice, Liver affection, Menstrual disorders, Paralysis, Testicles, Tumours affection of, Ulcers, Vertigo, etc.
SPHERES OF ACTION: The seat of action of this remedy is centred on the nervous system, particularly motor nerves first and later on the sensory nerves as well; heart, cardiovascular system, glands and female genital organs.

PATHOGENESIS

It powerfully depresses motor nerves leading to paralysis of the muscles of the body as far as voluntary and reflex motions are concerned. It causes paralysis of the motor nerve filaments of the cerebrospinal system. The sensory nerves, spinal cord and brain are affected later on. It depresses the vagus ganglia, resulting in fall of blood pressure and quick pulse, but lowers the temperature. Its effect on glands causes induration and hypertrophy.

CONSTITUTION

Make-up of the body: It is mostly suited to old men and women, old bachelors, during and after climacteric age. Persons having debility and diseases caused by blow or fall.

The strongest characteristic of Conium maculatum is its peculiar VERTIGO, which is much aggravated by TURNING THE HEAD SIDEWISE or LOOKING AROUND OR TURNING IN BED.

. Sweats day and night as soon as the patient sleeps or even when closing the eyes

(China, Thuja, Cactus rev. of Sambucus). Very offensive sweat.

. Swelling and induration of glands after contusion or bruise. . Cancerous and scrofulous persons with enlarged glands. . Intermittent flow of urine: great difficulty in passing urine; urine flows, stops and

flows again; from prostatic and uterine affections, or paretic conditions.

. Breast sore, hard and painful, especially during the menstrual period. . Objects look red, rainbow coloured, double vision, weakness of sight, aversion to

light without inflammation, but, with intense photophobia.

_ Desire for warmth especially of the sun, coffee, acid and salty food. . Aversion to open air, light, business, study, bread. Craving for salt, coffee and sour

things. Desire for warmth of sun. Cough when lying down, aggravated from slightest exposure to cold air.

Cold stool and flatulence is a unique characteristic of Coniummac. (Hot stool and flatulence, Sulphur). Ascending type of paralysis reminds of Conium.

Mind : The patient is morose and ill humoured and easily angered. He is very much quarrelsome and scolds always even at silly things.

The patient cannot and will not bear contradiction; excitement of any kind causes mental depression.

The patient has no inclination to business or to study; very much indifferent and indolent; does not take interest in anything.

Very forgetful; weak memory; is uanble to sustain and mental effort. Cannot bear to be alone; dread of being alone; yet avoids society (Kali carb., Lyco.).

Ailments from : Blow or fall, contusion, sexual excess, sexual abstinence or SUPPRESSED SEXUAL DESIRE: suppressed menses, excitement or over work.
PARTICULARS: Headache

Causation: Headache is caused by blow or fall, sexual excess, suppressed menses, excitement or over work, insufficient evacuation.

Location: Lancinating pain especially on the vertex and forehead, in temples; semi-lateral.

Sensation: Sensation as if there is much foreign substance in the head. Sensation as if the brain has gone to sleep.

Character of headache: Stupefying pains in the head; excessive sensibility of brain. Tearing and lancinating pain as if the head were beaten to pieces or the contents of skull would be pressed out. Stitching in head while coughing. Headache with numbness of the brain. Attack of tearing headache which compels the patient to lie down. Obstinate shooting pain in the sinciput; heaviness and squeezing sensation. Apoplexy with paralysis of old people.

Modalities

* Aggravation: When walking in the open air; from contact, motion and after eating.

* Amelioration: When lying in a recumbent position or while stooping; by external pressure and © Concomitants: Nausea and vomiting of mucus. Apoplexy with paralysis of old people.

Vertigo : The strongest characteristic of this drug, from the Homoeopathic point of view, IS ITS PECULIAR VERTIGO which aggravated by TURNING THE HEAD SIDEWISE OR TURNING IN THE BED, especially of old people. Feels as if bed were floating. Vertigo after intoxication even after taking a very small quantity. There is whirling Vertigo on rising and sometimes causes a fall, especially in the morning.

Eyes, eye troubles are caused by injury or blow and eye strain; or Using artificial lightly students; sexual excess or suppressed menses and sexual suppression.

Character of eye troubles: There is aversion to light without inflammation of eyes. Ophthalmia with intense photophobia. Weakness and dazzling of the eyes, with giddiness and debility. Weakness of vision. Pupils dilated, the pain is worse at night and terribly aggravated by least ray of light, relieved in a dark room and by pressure.

Gastro-intestinal tract :

Tongue : Tongue is swollen, painful, stiff and paralysed, Consequently, there is difficulty in speech. Bitter taste in the mouth.

Stomach : There is no appetite. Eructations taste sour arid offensive. Terrible nausea with violent vomiting like coffee-ground; acrid heartburn; worse on going to bed. Amelioration from eating, but aggravation a few hours after meals. Cutting pain in the abdomen as from a knife. Severe aching in and around liver. Rumbling with painful tightness of abdomen.

Stool : Cold stool and cold flatulence. Frequent ineffectual urging to stool; passes little at a time. Burning in rectum during stool. Stool is full of undigested matter and painless; passes involuntarily during sleep.

Urine : There is great difficulty in voiding urine; FLOW INTERMITS, STOPS AND THEN FLOWS

AGAIN. Flow stops on straining, from enlarged prostate, uterine affections or paretic conditions. Pain when urinating. Urine is pale with grey or white sediment.

name: Corallium Rubrum
author: Dubey
chapter: Dubey Text Book of Materia Medica

sections.title: INTRODUCTION
sections.content:
Red coral, the product of coralligene Zoophyte, contains carbonate of lime, Oxide of iron, gelatin and other elements. In old physic it was considered to have “strengthening properties” and to be astringent, sudorific, diuretic and absorbent.

Catarrh. Eruptions. Post nasal catarrh. Cough-whooping, hysterical & other types of eough.

1) “Minute gun cough” during the day and whooping cough at night.

2) Inspired air feels cold (Ars., Aesc., Brom.)

3) “Whooping cough or any other kind of cough when the attack comes on with a very rapid cough and the attack follows so closely as to almost run into each other”— Guernsey.

4) Violent paroxysm of cough with bleeding from mouth & nose.

5) Profuse secretion of mucus through the posterior nares obliging one to hawk frequently. (Nat. Garb.)

6) “Continuous hysterical cough”—Author has found it useful after Ignatia has failed.

7) Feels suffocated and greatly exhausted after whooping cough.

8) Skin : Red Flat ulcers. Coral-colored, then dark red spots, changing to copper colored spots. Psoriasis of palms & soles.

sections.title: PARTICULARS
sections.content:
Respiratory Symptoms : Nose : Post nasal catarrh. Profuse secretion of mucus dropping through posterior nares. Dry coryza; nose stopped up and ulcerated. Painful ulcers in nostrils. Odors of smoke, onions etc. °

Throat: Throat very sensitive, especially to air. Hawking of profuse mucus.

Chest: Dry spasmodic suffocative cough ; very rapid cough, short, barking. Cough with great sensitiveness of air passages. Feel cold on deep inspiration. Continuous hysterical cough. Patient feels suffocated and greatly exhausted after whooping cough. “Minute gun cough” during the day and whooping cough at night. Violent paroxysm of cough with bleeding from mouth & nose.

Complementary ; Sulph. Compare : Bell,, Dros., MephiU Caust,

name: Crataegus
author: Dubey
chapter: Dubey Text Book of Materia Medica
modalities:
Aggravation—In warm room, exertion or excitement. Amelioration—Fresh air, quiet and rest.

TONICS Heart Tonic—-Crataegus. Lung Tonic—Aspidosperma. Oldage Tonie—Avena Sativa. Children Tonic & Appetizer—China, Hydrastis, Chelido- nium, Gentiana Lutea. Sexual Tonie—Damiana.

sections.title: CLINICAL
sections.content:
Angina pectoris. Heart- affection of.

Crataegus was introduced into medicine as a heart remedy by Dr. Greene of Ennis, Ireland. Crataegus is useful in those desperate cases of heart affections such as valvular deficien-cies of hypertrophy where dyspnoea and dropsy have super-vened, and the pulse is gradually growing weak and rapid where physicians have lost heart.

There is extreme dyspnoea on least exertion without much increase of pulse. Pain in region of. heart and under left clavicle. Heart dilated ; first sound weak— pulse acceler-ated, irregular, feeble intermittent. There may be extreme weakness, general anaSarca, insomnia, anaemia, cutaneous chilliness with heart disease.

name: Crocus Sativus
author: Dubey
chapter: Dubey Text Book of Materia Medica

sections.title: INTRODUCTION
sections.content: One of the richest and very useful remedy of the Vegetable kingdom belonging to the family Iridaceae, is Crocus sativus, commonly named as saffron. Saffron is used frequently as a Condiment. It bears an individual characteristic, being brick-red in colour which, on proving produces haemorrhages of DARKISH RED hue. Of course, brightness may also be an occasional feature. VISCIDITY AND STRINGINESS are the other two characteristics of its blood picture.

sections.title: CLINICAL
sections.content: Brain affection, Chorea, Eye affection, Epistaxis, Headache, Haemorrhage, Heart troubles, Hysteria, Laughter, Lachrymotion, Menstrual disorders, Nose affection, Opthalmia, Threatened abortion, etc.

sections.title: SPHERES OF ACTION
sections.content:
It acts especially upon the female genital organs, but eyes, chest and abdomen may also be affected in rare instances. Brain and mind too are important centres for its action.

It causes chorea and hysteria. Acting on female genital organs; it causes abortion and produces HAEMORRHAGE, THE BLOOD BEING DARK, STRINGY AND CLOTTED.

CONSTITUTION There is no particular constitution of the patient as such. The patient is however,

having syphilitic background, HAEMORRHAGIC DIATHESIS and of nervous and hysterical temperament.

sections.title: GUIDING SYMPTOMS
sections.content:
1. Frequent and extreme changes in sensation; sudden, from the greatest hilarity to the deepest despondency. (Ign., Nux mos., Platina) anger with violence rapidly followed by repentance, laughter quickly succeeded by tears,

2. Haemorrhage from any and every orifice of the body which IS DARK, VISCID, pied orn IN LONG BLACK STRINGS, HANGING FROM THE BLEEDING RFACE.

243

sections.title: PARTICULARS
sections.content:
Eyes

Sensation in the eyes as if the room were filled with smoke, as if he had been violently weeping. A constant desire to wink and wipe the eyes with a feeling as though a film of mucus were over the eyes. The vision seems dim as though the whole room were full of smoke or as if cold wind is blowing across the eyes.

Lachrymation on reading. Tears rushes out from the dim eyes as soon as he begins to read. The lachrymation occurs only when the patient is in the room and not when he is in the open air.

There is itching in the eyelids, pain as from excoriation and sensation of burning in the eyes and eyelids, especially when closing them or while reading.

Nose

Epistaxis only from one nostril at a time. Nose bleeds. The character of blood is BLACK, VISCID, CLOTTED, FORMING INTO LONG, BLACK STRINGS, HANGING FROM THE NOSE, every drop can be turned into a thread with cold sweat in large drops on forehead.

Female genital organs

Menses. Crocus is suited for DYSMENORRHOEA AND METRORRHAGIA. Time: Too early, Quantity: Too profuse.

Character of blood: Dark, stringy, viscid, clotted, forming long black strings, hangs from the bleeding surface: rush of blood to genitals.

name: Crotalus Horridus
author: Dubey
chapter: Dubey Text Book of Materia Medica

sections.title: INTRODUCTION
sections.content:
The first regular proving of this drug was made by Hering and by others under his personal direction. It is prepared from the venom of the deadly Rattle Snake of North America, Dr. Tyler remarks to “Homoeopathic specifics” in her Drug Picture. There are drugs whose malignant effects on human body present an almost perfect picture of some diseases and can be used as specific for that particular symptom syndrome; examples being:

Crotalus horridus and Black Water Fever.

Arsenic and Ptomaine poisoning, Merc. cor. and Dysentery. Belladonna and Scarlet Fever.

Even Master Hahnemann has said, “Where such correspondence occurs we have specifics.” Hence it is seen that Crotalus horridus is in intimate relation with the signs and symptoms of blood poisoning manifesting AS BLACK WATER FEVER, with characteristic haemorrhages here and there.

sections.title: CLINICAL
sections.content: Apoplexy, Boils, Cancer, Carbuncles, Convulsion, Diarrhoea, Diphtheria, Delirium, Dyspepsia, Ecchymosis, Epilepsy, Eye effection, Erysipelas, Fever, Haemorrhoids, Headache, Heart affection, Jaundice, Liver affections, Lung trouble, Meningitis, Menstrual disorders, Skin affection, Tongue affection, Ulcers, Vomiting, Whooping cough, etc.

sections.title: SPHERES OF ACTION
sections.content:
It acts primarily upon cerebrospinal nerve centres and secondarily upon the fibrin of blood and liver.

PATHOGENESIS

It causes DECOMPOSITION OF BLOOD AND PRODUCES HAEMORRHAGE FROM ALL ORIFICES OF THE BODY e.g. eyes, ears, nose, mouth, throat and urethra. It also acts upon cerebro-spinal nerve centres producing rapid and direct depressing

Haemorrhagic diathesis: blood flows from eyes, ears, nose and every orifice of the body and even pores of the skin; blood being fluid, dark, non-coagulable and offensive.

. Malignant jaundice, haematic rather than hepatic. . Mostly affects right side of the body.

. Bad effects of vaccination, especially blood poisoning as a result. . There is general aggravation in the morning on waking or aggravation wakes the

patient up at night.

. Tongue fiery red; smooth: and polished (Pyr., Fer. met., Apis), intensely swollen,

difficulty in swallowing.

. Purpura haemorrhagica: sudden bleeding from all orifice skin, nails, gums, etc. . Low spetie condition with blood decomposition.

Black, coffee-ground and offensive stool. There is desire for stimulants and aversion to meat.

13. Aliments from : Fright, sun, alcohol, foul water, and vaccination.

name: Croton Tiglium
author: Dubey
chapter: Dubey Text Book of Materia Medica

sections.title: INTRODUCTION
sections.content: Croton tig. is a very valuable remedy prepared from croton oil seed, having a limited range of action in therapeutic sphere. Mostly it is a remedy for the relief of acute troubles. Nevertheless, no other drug in Hemoeopathic Materia Medica is able to replace it for its peculiar affinity to mucous membrane of gastro- intestinal tract and skin and thus the indispensability of this remedy has been well established.

sections.title: CLINICAL
sections.content: Cholera, Colds, Cough, Diarrhoea, Breast affection, Ear affection, Eczema, Skin affection, etc.

sections.title: SPHERES OF ACTION
sections.content:
It acts especially on mucous membrane of gastro-intestinal tract and skin. Respiratory organs are also within the domain of action of this remedy.

It produces both irritation and inflammation of skin, resulting in formation of vesicles and mucus discharge. Burning in oesophagus is one of its metastatic pathological actions. It also causes congestion of gastro-intestinal tract, copious watery stool and peritonitis. Hyperaemia of the glandular system too is within its range of action.

1. Profuse watery diarrhoea “coming out like a shot” as soon as the patient eats and drinks, followed by great prostration. The evacuation is yellowish or yellowish green.

2. On the skin Croton produces ERYTHEMA, ERYSIPELAS, ECZEMA, HERPES, PUSTULES, etc. There is intense itching of the skin but the patient cannot bear to scratch very hard as it hurts; a very slight scratch or a mere rub suffice to allay the

3. Touch pressure and motion aggravate, Aggravation at night and summer.

4. Suffocating cough as soon as the head touches the pillow (Hyos., Drosera, Rumex, Belladonna, Conium).

5. Drawing pain through the chest from nipple to scapula of the same side when child nurses (Nipple to all over body—Phytolacca; nipple to uterus—Puls., Silicea).

- Aggravation from eating and drinking and from every movement, followed by great Prostration.

251

sections.title: PARTICULARS
sections.content:
Diarrhoea

Causation: Fron fruits, _Sweet-meat. and hot summer weather. Before stool: There is is swashing sensation in intestine as from water, and colic before diarrhoea. During stool: Constant urging to stool, followed by SUDDEN EVACUATION. The bowels are moved as if by “SPASMODIC JERKS, COMING OUT LIKE A SHOT”.

Character of stool: Gushing of thin, yellow, watery stool, profuse in quantity, is the striking feature of Croton tig.

Concomitants: With stool, the stomach is greatly distended and very much sensitive to touch with much gurgling in bowels.

Modality: Aggravation from eating, drinking or even while eating and summer.

Cough

Cough especially at night, often compelling the patient to rise from a sound sleep.

Character of cough: Violent spasmodic with dyspnoea, choking, more at night, obliging the patient to sit up. Sensitive to deep breathing.

Extreme irritation of air passage, so that the inhalation of air brings on cough. Modality; Cough aggravated from lying down, as soon as the head touches the pillow at night.

Breast

There is drawing pain through the chest from breast to scapula of the same side, every time the child nurses. (Pain extends from nipple all over—Phytolacca; from nipple to uterus—Puls., Silicea)

Skin

Eczema all over the body, especially of scalp and genital organs, either-purely vesicular or pustular. The vesicles dry up and are followed by red, raw, inflamed surface.

Intense itching of skin, but it is so tender that the patient is unable to scratch, instead rubs gently te get relief, There is also severe itching on genitals in both sexes which may be vesicular or pustular but very much sensitive and sore but gentle rubbing gives relief and comfort.

General Modalities : Aggravation: Diarrhoea by every motion, from eating and drinking, even while eating the least food and drink.

Relations

Antidoes: Rhus tox. Antidoted by: Antim. tart.

name: Cuprum Metallicum
author: Dubey
chapter: Dubey Text Book of Materia Medica

sections.title: INTRODUCTION
sections.content: Metallic copper, an insoluble substance when it is pure, is made soluble by means of trituration. It was Master. Hahnemann who solved this problem of using insoluble substance, in the field of therapeutics. This medicine was first introduced by him as one of the weapons for the then prevailing cholera epidemic. By the members of the orthodox school, copper is used as copper sulphate for therapeutic purposes, especially for external application. They did not dare to use it internally because of its chemically poisonous effect, but Homoeopathy has made it useful through the process of trituration.

sections.title: CLINICAL
sections.content: Angina pectoris, Asthma, Cholera, Chorea, Convulsion, Cough, Cramps, Croup, Cyanosis, Dyspnoea, Epilepsy Gastric disorders, Gout, Throat affection, Measles, Meningitis, Neuralgia, Paralysis, Spasm, Whooping cough, etc.

sections.title: SPHERES OF ACTION
sections.content:
Cuprum met. acts prominently upon the alimentary canal and profoundly influences the nervous system and various nerve centres.

PATHOGENESIS

Cuprum met. causes gastro-intestinal inflammation, colic, diarrhoea and vomiting. Acting on the nerve centres it gives rise to SPASMODIC AFFECTIONS CRAMPS,

paralysis, convulsions, beginning in fingers and toes; violent contractive and intermitting pain with tonic and clonic spasm etc.

CONSTITUTION

Physical make-up: “It is suited to fair haired people and the carbo-nitrogenoid constitution, women who have borne many children” (Clarke).

Relation with heat and cold: Symptoms are aggravated from cold air.

Miasm: It is an anti-psoric remedy WORKING FROM WITHIN OUTWARDS.

sections.title: GUIDING SYMPTOMS
sections.content: 1. It ranks with most important medicines for troubles arising from the “STRIKING INWARD” of diseases of failure of eruptions or discharges to come out or

sections.title: PARTICULARS
sections.content:
Respiratory Symptoms :

Cough : Cuprum met. is a favourite remedy in whooping cough. The attacks are SPASMODIC in nature.

Sensation: Cough with a gurgling sound in the throat as if water is being poured out of a bottle.

Character of cough: The cough is so long lasting and suffocative that the patient turns entirely breathless, blue and rigid. While coughing, the face becomes, livid or blue. The finger nails become discoloured,.the eyes are turned up and the patient coughs until he loses breath.

There is also rattling in the chest. Whenever the respiratory organs are affected, there is spasmodic breathing and dyspnoea; more the dyspnoea, more likely is it that the thumbs will be clenched and the fingers cramped. Cough in three paroxysms successively, the patient is unable to speak; becomes breathless; blue faced, rigid and stiff, cataleptic spasm with each paroxysm.

At the end of cough, he vomits out all the food taken plus a little quantity of tough gelatinous mucus. Modality: Worse at 3 a.m. Better by drinking cold water (Causticum).

Cholera

In cholera morbus or Asiatic cholera, Cuprum met. Is an excellent remedy. Its application is generally

confined to the later part of the second stage and the early part of the third stage of the disease. When the CRAMP STARTS AND COLLAPSE BEGINS TO APPEAR, Cuprum met. is well indicated.

name: Cyclamen Europaeum
author: Dubey
chapter: Dubey Text Book of Materia Medica

sections.title: INTRODUCTION
sections.content: Cyclamen has a traditional reputation as a remedy for affections of the uterus and appendages. The later oprovings have demonstrated the correctness of this. It is in many ways analogous to Pulsatilla, from which it differs mainly in having no better from open air ; and in not having thirstlessness as so frequent an accompaniment of other conditions.

sections.title: CLINICAL
sections.content:
Acne. Anaemia. Chlorosis. Dyspepsia. Eyes affections. Headache. Heel pain. Menstrual disorder. Mental. Pruritus. Rheumatism.

SPHERE OF ACTION & PATHOGENESIS

It acts upon cerebro-spinal system affecting sensorium, eyes, gastrointestinal canal and more especially female sexual system.

CONSTITUTION

Physical make up—Best adapted to blonde leuco-phlegmatic who are pale and anaemic. Temperament: Phlegmatic and irritable temperament. Heat cold relation : Chilly patient. Miasm : Psoric and sycotic miasms are in the back ground.

sections.title: GUIDING SYMPTOMS
sections.content:
1) Aversion to open air : The patient dreads open air (coryza and cough relief in open air).

2) Deranged Menses in pale, chlorotic women : attended with headache, vertigo and dim vision.

3) Weeping disposition : The patient is mentally sad, irrit-able, peevish, morose and desires to be alone.

4) Thirstlessness : There is no thirst all day but it occurs in the evening during fever.

5) (a) Desire: For lemonade, (Bell., Nit. Acid., Pills,, Sabina., Sec-Cor.) Inedible things (Calc. Os., Cina., Cicuta., Psorinum etc.) (b) Aversion : To fat, meat, bread & butter. Ordinary food and beer. Pork disagrees. (c) Appetite : Satiety after a few mouthfuls (Lye.) and then he loathes food which causes nausea, (d) Taste : Saliva and all food taste salty.

author: Dubey
chapter: Dubey Text Book of Materia Medica

sections.title: INTRODUCTION
sections.content:
This is another excellent remedy from the vegetable kingdom, usually indicated in heart diseases. This is a wild plant grown best in siliceous soil in bushy grounds and waste places of Europe. The fresh leaves from this uncultivated plant are gathered, and from this the mother tincture is prepared and subsequent potencies are made.

Angina pectoris, Asthma, Bright’s disease, Cyanosis, Delirium, Diarrhoea, Dropsy, Headache, Heart affection, Lung troubles, Urinary troubles, etc.

sections.title: SPHERES OF ACTION
sections.content:
Its main seat of action is heart and circulation, gastro-intestinal tract and uro-genital organs.

Its action through cardiac peripheral end of vagus inhibits the activity of heart, resulting in SLOW HEART BEAT; prolonged diastole and rise of blood pressure. It also

causes suppression of urine producing oedema. It is also capable of irritating gastro- intestinal tract, producing vomiting and diarrhoea.

CONSTITUTION

There is no particular constitution or make-up of the body as such. However, the patient is light-haried scrofulous; children of fair complexion and people of climacfric age having weak heart, but without valvular complicaions. Blueness of the skin, with cyanosis of eye-lids, lips, tongue and nails.

Relation with heat and cold: Chilly patient with great sensitiveness to cold air and cold weather; cold food and drink which aggravate.

Miasm: Psora and Sycosis are in the background,

Diathesis: Scrofulous diathesis.

sections.title: GUIDING SYMPTOMS
sections.content:
1. Prostration from slight exertion. 2. Sensation as if the heart would stop beating if she moved (rev-Gels.). 3. Motion aggravates most of its complaints.

4.

Slow and weak, irregular, intermittent pulse; intermitting every 3rd, 5th and 7th beat.

. Enlarged, sore and painful liver.

6. White and pasty stool.

10.

. Blueness of the skin, with cyanosis of face, eyelids, lips, tongue and nails, face is cold

and pale and is covered with cold sweat.

. Great weakness and deadly sinking in epigastrium with nausea and vomiting from smell of food; clean tongue and great thirst.

. Respiration is very difficult and he often takes deep breath.

Mind : There is great anxiety and apprehension. The patient is very much despondent and fearful. Music is unbearable. It aggravates all troubles.

The patient is very much forgetful. His memory is weak and thinking is difficult.

11. Ailments from : Alcohol, high living, sexual excess and tobacco.

sections.title: PARTICULARS
sections.content:
Headache

Causation: Alcohol, tobacco, and sexual excess.

Location: Forehead and temples.

Sensation: Sudden cracking sensation in the head.

Character: Throbbing headache in the forehead, with stitches in forehead and temples.

Modalities: Aggravated by sitting erect, motion, music, excitement and eating.

Amelioration by pressrue, frequent profuse micturition. When the stomach is empty and in open air. Concomitants; Vertigo with anxiety and faintness.

Sensation: Sudden sensation as if the heart would stop beating if the patient moved (Fears unless constantly on the move, the heart would cease beating—Gels.).

Character: Weak heart without any valvular complications. There is uneasiness in the region of the

heart and precordium. IRREGULAR INTERMITTENT PULSE, generally occurring at climacteric age, aggravated by least motion, Heart's action is feeble. Heart beats more frequently, but intermits; sometimes irregular, VERY SLOW AND WEAK, INTERMITTING EVERY 3RD, 5TH AND 7TH BEAT. Frightful stiches in region of heart, coming on every fifteen minutes, lasting only five or six seconds each time (Angina pectoris).

name: Dioscorea Villosa
author: Dubey
chapter: Dubey Text Book of Materia Medica

sections.title: INTRODUCTION
sections.content: As a remedy for many kinds of pain, especially colic, and in severe, painful affections of abdominal and pelvic viscera, Dioscorea ranks with the polychrests of the Materia Medica. The pains of Dioscorea are neuralgic in character. It affects the ganglionic nervous system particularly of the umbilical region, thereby producing symptoms simulating an attack of bilious colic. Dr. Burt/ who made a heroic proving of this remedy, says—The grand sphere for the use of Dioscorea is among neuroses of the bowels and stomach; where the coeliac and umbilical plexuses are in a state of great hyperaesthesia, (the pain and spasm being unbearable. So whatever may be its action) It is one of the leading remedies for various kinds of colic, such as biliary, intestinal, flatulent, menstrual or renal when symptoms agree.

sections.title: CLINICAL
sections.content: Angina pectoris. Colic : Biliary, Intestinal, Renal, Flatulent, Menstrual, Gastralgia. Paronychia. Sciatica. Spermatorrhoea. Whitlow.

sections.title: SPHERES OF ACTION & PATHOGENESIS
sections.content: It chiefly acts on gastroin-testinal tract, liver, genito urinary organs and nervous system.

sections.title: GUIDING SYMPTOMS
sections.content:
1) Colic pains worse from bending forward and while lying; better on standing erect or bending backwards (Rev.of Col.)

2) Violent twisting colic, occurring in regular paroxysms, as if intestines were grasped and twisted by a powerful hand. There is gripping pains in abdomen about

3) Persons of feeble digestive powers, often subject to vio-lent colic; tea drinkers with much flatulence after meals or after eating.

4) Pains radiate from abdomen to back, chest, arms-r suddenly shift to different parts, appear in remote localities such as fingers and toes.

5) Disposition to paronychia, early stage of felons when pains are sharp and agonizing, when pricking is first felt, nails brittle.

name: Diphtherinum
author: Dubey
chapter: Dubey Text Book of Materia Medica

sections.title: INTRODUCTION
sections.content: Diphtherinum is prepared like all nosodes and animal poisons, according to the Homoeopathic Pharmacopoeia and like all homoeopathic remedies, is entirely safe when given to the sick. Like all the nosodes it is practically worthless in potencies below the 30th, its cura-tive value also increases with increases of potency from the 200th to the M and C.M. It need not and should not be repeated too frequently. It will cure in every case that crude antitoxin will and is not only easy to administer but also safe and entirely free from dangerous sequellae. Besides, it is homoeopathic. Dr. H.C. Allen had used it for twenty five years as a prophylactic and had never known a second case of diphtheria to occur in a family after it had been administered, The profession is asked to put it to the test and publish the failures to the world.

sections.title: CLINICAL
sections.content:
Croup. Diphtheria. Post diphtheritic paralysis. Epistaxis. Tonsillitis. Myelitis.

CONSTITUTION

Especially adapted to scrofulous, psoric or tuberculous persons, prone to catarrhal affections of throat and respiratory mucous membranes. Persons with weak or exhausted vitality are hence extremely susceptible to the diphtheritic virus. Diathesis—Especially adapted to strumous diathesis.

author: Dubey
chapter: Dubey Text Book of Materia Medica

sections.title: INTRODUCTION
sections.content:
It is a drug prepared from vegetable kingdom. It was first introduced by our

Master Hahnemann, but mastered equally well by Dr. Tyler as she remarks in her Drug Picture in the following words. “A few years ago, I came to the startling conclusion that the only two people

who really knew anything about Drosera were Samuel Hahnemann

and myself.” She proved her statement in

her subsequent writings when she unfolded the therapeutic effects of this wonderful drug in the sphere of respiratory affections, particularly the tubercular infection. Later on, clinical experiences confirmed that Drosera is not a drug with its spheres of action to whooping cough only but is capable of fighting the tubercular infection too, particularly of bones and glands.

sections.title: SPHERES OF ACTION
sections.content:
Acts markedly upon the respiratory organs by its influence on the pneum o-gastric nerve. It also affects bones and glands.

PATHOGENESIS It produces spasmodic dry cough; stimulating whooping cough. Drosera can break down resistance to tuberculosis and should, therefore, be capable of raising it (Dr.Tyler). 8. Violent spasmodic, frequent spell of barking cough, aggravated at night, after midnight, warmth, drinking, singing, laughing, weeping and LYING DOWN.

Cough : Suited especially in WHOOPING cough with violent paroxysms which follow one another rapidly.

Spasmodic cough with gagging, retching and vomiting.

During cough, there is vomiting of water, mucus and often bleeding from nose and mouth.

Violent tickling in the larynx brings on cough, makes the patient get up from sleep, coming on every few hours.

There is spasmodic difficulties of chest and larynx, causing difficult breathing and suffocation.

Sensation as if something in the chest preventing breathing when talking or coughing.

The face becomes purple from spasms in larynx with suffocation. Severe attack of stitching in the

chest when sneezing. Compression of the chest. Burning sensation in the chest, stitching pain in the chest.

With cough there is copious sweat all over the body.

There is severe hoarseness with sore throat.

Sensation: Constriction and crawling sensation in the throat, tickling as from a feather like sensation in the larynx.

Character: en's sore throat with rough, dry, scraping sensation in deep fauces. Voice is hoarse, deep, toneless, . requires great exertion to speak. The hoarseness and continued irritation cause coughing and scraping of the larynx.

Drosera is especially suited in phthisical condition of the lungs and larynx.

Character of pain: With cough, there |s stitching pain in the chest. The patient must hold the chest with both the hands to get relief.

Character of sputa: During coughing, there Is bleeding from various orifices, especially from the nose, throat, larynx and chest. Bloody saliva and haemorrhage from the mouth with bloody or purulent sputa. During coughing there is blue face with spasm of extremities.

Modality: Aggravation from talking, laughing, singing, and after mid-night.

name: Dulcamara
author: Dubey
chapter: Dubey Text Book of Materia Medica

sections.title: INTRODUCTION
sections.content: For this important drug and its exact and scientific use, we owe gratitude to our Master Hahnemann, It was regarded by him as “a very powerful plant” and he says that its duration of action is a long one. “Before the scientific proving of the drug was made”, remarked Kent “our mothers used to make ointments of Dulecamara for its astonishing, soothing effects on smarting wounds over the skin surface”. This effect has been proved and established rationally by a dozen of provers whom Hahnemann employed.

sections.title: CLINICAL
sections.content: Anasarco, Catarrh, Bladder affection, Cough, Cholera, Diarrhoea, Dropsy, Dysentery, Fevers, Headache, Herpes, Influenza, Lumbago, Measles, Meningitis, Nettle rash, Neuralgia, Ophthalmia, Nose affection, Skin troubles, Tonsillitis, Urinary affection, Warts, Whooping cough, etc.

sections.title: SPHERES OF ACTION
sections.content:
Dulcamara affects subversively as well as curatively all mucous membranes, besides glands, skin and muscles.

PATHOGENESIS

It causes glandular enlargement, especially of the lymphatic system, cellular effusion and produces skin eruptions. It also produces catarrhal inflammation of mucous membrane and skin, resulting in profuse secretion-of mucous membrane and skin.

CONSTITUTION Physical make-up : Especially suited to persons of phlegmatic scrofulous constitution. Temperament: Irritable temperament.

Relation with heat and cold: Neither chilly not hot. Easily affected by sudden change from heat to cold or from cold to wet rainy weather.

Miasm: Sycotic and Psoric patient.

sections.title: GUIDING SYMPTOMS
sections.content:
1. Duleamara is an excellent remedy for the troubles BROUGHT ON OR AGGRAVATED BY EXPOSURE TO COLD DAMP RAINY WEATHER,

—

270

sections.title: PARTICULARS
sections.content:
Headache

Causation: From exposure to cold, getting wet in rain, damp cold weather, etc.

Character of headache: There is occipital headache ascending from the nape of neck. There is digging pain in forehead, with sensation as if the brain were too large. Stupefying pain in back part of the head. Back of the head is chilly, heavy and aching during cold weather.

Headache is relieved by talking.

Concomitants: Along with headache, there may be vertigo, especially on walking in the morning or when rising from bed.

Eyes

Causation: Cold, every time the patient takes cold, It settles in the eyes.

Due to catarrhal condition there is profuse discharge from the eyes.

Character of discharge: Thick, yellowish, profuse, discharges with granular lids, every time he takes cold.

Modalities: Aggravation from open air, cold damp weather. Amelioration in closed room.

Nose

Causation; From cold damp weather.

sections.title: CLINICAL
sections.content:
Cystitis. Dropsy. Enuresis. Gravel Haematuria.

Gonorrhoea. Gleet. Urine-retention of.

The chief effects of Equisetum are found in the urinary > organs, it principally acts an urinary bladder. It is very popu-lar remedy for enuresis, gonorrhoea, gleet, haematuria, gravel and dropsy. Its indications are as follows :—

1) Frequent & intolerable urging to urinate, with severe pain at close of urination (Barb., Sars., Thuja)

2) Constant desire to urinate; passes large quantity of clear watery urine without relief.

3) Severe dull pain the bladder, as from distension not relieved after

4) Sharp, burning, cutting pain in urethra while urinating.

5) Enuresis day & night (Arg Nit., Caust.) with profuse watery urine of unknown cause.

6) Incontience in children with dreams or nightmares when passing urine and in old women.

7) Retention and dysuria during pregnancy and after deliv-ery.

8) Deep pain in the region of right kidney extending to lower abodomen with urgent desire to micturate.

Modéalities : Agg. : Right side, movement, pressure, bouch, sitting down. Amel : In afternoon, from lying down.

name: Erigeron Canadensis
author: Dubey
chapter: Dubey Text Book of Materia Medica

sections.title: CLINICAL
sections.content:
Bruises. Dysuria. gleet. Gonorrhoea. Haemorrhages. Placenta praevia. Wounds. Dysentery. Bladder affection of.

Erigeron is chiefly known as a remedy for haemorrhages and congestions in all parts of the body. Haemorrhages are caused and cured by this remedy. The haemorrhage of this remedy, it is immaterial from what orifice it may take place : is characterised by the bright redness of the blood (Mill., Trill.). It can be used with great advantages in cases of haematemesis due to ulceration or rupture of blood vessels in the stomach, in epistaxis, haemorrhage from the bowels may be due to fissures, metrorrhagia and menorrhagia from urinary bladder, chronic cystitis, polyp & malignancy etc. Haemorrhage from the uterus, bloody lochia even leucor-rhoea are usually attended with painful micturition or urinary irritation and in some cases with irritation of the rectum.

. i" Se we

é . wy : g. td. ee oe

Dr. Moore used Erigenon in several cases of placenta praevia where the indications were profuse flow of bright red blood, pallor, weakness, and an aggravation of the flow from the slightest movement on the part of the patient.

Author has found this remedy very useful in checking the haemorrhage from urinary bladder than any other remedy. It may be due to chronic cystitis, polyp or malignant condition.

Female : This remedy is indicated in metrorrhagia menorrhagia, leucorrhoea and prolapsus uteri etc. Usually when associated with violent irritation of bladder & rectum. Bright red flow. Bloody lochia returns after least motion & comes in gushes. Pregnant women with “Weak uterus”. Nosebleed instead of menses.

name: Eupatorium Perfoliatum
author: Dubey
chapter: Dubey Text Book of Materia Medica

sections.title: INTRODUCTION
sections.content:
Commonly known as Boneset or Ague-weed, Eupatorium perfoliatum is a remedy with which every Homoeopath is more or less familiar especially in the management of acute fevers like Dengue, Influenza, Malaria, etc. In regard to its common name “Boneset”, DR. N.M. CHOUDHURY SAYS “The name Boneset is very apt in as much as it conveys to the mind the supreme characteristic of the drug viz., it soothes painful bone. So important is this symptom that its absence may be regarded as a contra-indication for Eupatorium”.

Bilious fever, Bone pains, Cough, Dengue, Influenza, Intermittent fever, Soreness, Headache, Rheumatism, etc.

sections.title: SPHERES OF ACTION
sections.content:
Eupatorium perfoliatum acts principally upon the gastro-hepatic organs and bronchial mucous membrane and fibrous tissue. PATHOGENESIS

It produces, as one of its most characteristic conditions, bilious derangement with tenderness of hepatic region and vomiting of bile. It also produces sorenss and aching of muscles and bones which accompany some forms of febrile diseases like malaria and influenza.

CONSTITUTION

There is no particular constitution as such of this patient. However, the remedy is more adapted to diseases of people, having worn out constitution due to excessive abuse of aleohol, cachexia, from prolonged or frequent attacks of bilious or intermittent fevers.

sections.title: GUIDING SYMPTOMS
sections.content:
1. Brusised feeling as if broken all over the body (Arn., Pyrogen, Ham.).

2. Bone pains of all description appear in the remedy, Pains affecting back, head, chest, limbs, especially the wrists which feel as if dislocated. The more general and severe the pain, better the remedy is indicated and adapted.

276

sections.title: PARTICULARS
sections.content:
Headache

Time: Periodical headache, every 3rd or 7th day. Location: Pain at the base of brain. Sensation: Congestive type of headache. Sensation as if head is going to burst.

Character of pain: Throbbibg pain in the head, pressure as if a cap of lead pressed over the whole skull; extreme soreness of the head.

Modality: Aggravation after lying down. Concomitants: Vertigo with headache, sensation as if falling to the left.

Respiratory Symptoms : Cough : Chronic loose cough with coryza and sneezing. * Causation : From suppressed intermittent fever or after measles. * Sensation : Cough excited by tickling in the chest, causing tightness of the chest.

* Character of cough : Hawking cough with difficulty in breathing; while coughing the patient must support the chest with hands.

* Character of sputa : With cough, there is scanty expectoration.

+ * Character of pain : Sharp pain through right chest on deep inspiration and with SORENESS HEST,

* Modality : Aggravation from lying on back, from Inspiration, relieved by lying on hands and

Extremities : In chronic cases of gout and rheumatism this medicine is of great help. * Causation: After malarial fever.

3. The eyes water all the time and are agglutinated in morning

6. Profuse offensive expectoration of mucus by voluntary hawking.

7. Bad effects from fall, contusion, or mechanical injuries of external parts of the eye,

8. Aggravation in the evening, WARMTH and indoors,

—___

sections.title: PARTICULARS
sections.content:
Headache

Euphrasia commonly has cattarrhal headache. Sensation: As if the head is going to burst.

Nose

Great sneezing and PROFUSE FLUENT CORYZA; the nasal mucous membrane is swollen. The discharge is BLAND and it occurs with ACRID LACHRYMATION.

name: Ferrum Metallicum
author: Dubey
chapter: Dubey Text Book of Materia Medica

sections.title: INTRODUCTION
sections.content: The metallic iron suggests anaemia to many common people as well as to medical men. Iron plays a vital role in the manifestation of anaemia; hence the word “FERRUM” is invariably associated with “ANAEMIA” and vice versa by orthodox school of medicine. WHAT ZINCUM IS TO NERVES, THE SAME, IRON IS TO BLOOD. Ferrum was proved by Hahnemann who said, “most of the provings of iron were observed from the employment of the solution of the actuals of iron, yet the symptoms correspond to those of the metallic iron.”

sections.title: CLINICAL
sections.content: Aneamia, Asthma, Abdominal disorders, Chlorosis, Cough, Cramps, Constipation, Chorea, Convulsion, Diarrhoea, Dropsy, Fever, Goitre, Haemorrhage, Headache, Menstrual disorders, Rheumatism, Vertige. Whooping Cough, etc.

sections.title: SPHERES OF ACTION
sections.content:
Iron has chief action on the blood element, HAEMOGLOBIN OF R.B.C., skin and muscular tissues of the body are acted upon later after the blood has been primarily affected. Gastro intestinal tract and uterus are the other seats of action.

Iron has an important place as a constituent of haemoglobin. Initially iron increases the R.B.C. count causing FALSE PLETHORA but later on it produces anaemia. A disturbance of the equilibrium causes relaxation. The vessels walls dilate resulting in congestion, increased blood pressure and haemorrhage. In alimentary canal, peristalsis is weakened, producing vomiting, constipation, diarrhoea, etc.

CONSTITUTION

Physical make-up: Especially adapted to women who are PALE, weak, delicate and chlorotic, yet have a FIERY RED FACE,

Temperament: Sanguine temperament easily vexed, least contradiction excites the patient.

Relation with heat and cold: Hot patient.

sections.title: GUIDING SYMPTOMS
sections.content:
1. Any RAPID EXERTION OR MOTION brings on weakness, dyspnoea, sinking and 2.A strange symptom running through Ferrum is that the PAINS AND SUFFERINGS COME ON DURING REST, such as palpitation, dyspnoea and

weakness. That is why the patient is ameliorated by MOVING ABOUT GENTLY in the house or in open air.

3. Complaints from LOSS OF VITAL FLUID as is China especially from haemorrhage.

4. EXTRENE PALENESS of the face, lips and mucus membrane which become red and flushed on least pain, emotion or exertion.

5. Red parts become white.

6. Haemorrhage from anywhere and everywhere; the character of the blood is BRIGHT RED COAGULABLE.

7. Profound prostration with general anaemia, but with tendency to flushing of face and head with headache.

8. Emaciation, weakness and trembling in frequent attacks. 9. Canine hunger or alternate loss of appetite with dislike for any food. 10. Dropsy due to loss of vital fluid, abuse of quinine, suppressed intermittents, etc. 11. Desire for bread; aversion to eggs, meat, milk, beer and sour things (Craving for eggs—Calc. carb.). 12. Fiery red tongue (Apis., Crot. hor, Pyr.). 13. Ailments from : Loss of vital fluid, abuse of quinine, suppressed intermittents, etc.

sections.title: PARTICULARS
sections.content:
Headache

Causation: Loss of vital fluid, abuse of quinine and suppressed intermittents. Time: Periodic type of headache, every 2,3 or 4 days or every 2 or 3 weeks.

Character of pain: Hammering, beating, pulsating type of pain in head. Congestive type of headache, pain in the back of head. Pain compels the patient to lie down:

Modalities: Aggravation by coughing and amelioration by pressure and Slow walking about.

Concomitants: With headache, there is vertigo with balancing sensation as if on water; also there may be aversion to eating and drinking.

Vertigo

When there is vertigo, the patient feels a peculiar sensation of balancing, as if on water, or the vertigo appears on seeing flowing water, or as if walking over water when crossing a bridge, or on descending.

author: Dubey

sections.title: INTRODUCTION
sections.content: It is one of organic tissue salts introduced by Schussler. Its function is to lend colour or pigment to the blood corpuscles. It also carries oxygen to all parts of the body. The deficiency in this cell salt leads to disturbance of circulation. Disturbed circulation again in its trend causes other disturbances in the normal equilibrium of the human system. This remedy needs thorough proving for detail symptomatology. The symptoms available are derived from the writings of Schussler, proving by J. C. Margan & some clinical experiences of homoeopathic practitioners.

sections.title: CLINICAL
sections.content: Debility, Ear-affections of, Epistaxis, Fever, Headache; Haematuria, Haemoptysis. Haemor-rhages. Inflammations. Injuries, Pleurisy, Pneumonia, Rheumatism. Urine- incotinece of, varicose veins.

sections.title: SPHERES OF ACTION & PATHOGENESIS
sections.content:
The main action of this drug is on relaxed muscular tissue and the blood corpuscles.

GUIDING SYMPTOMES

1) First stage of all febrile disturbances and inflammations before exudation sets in.

2) In the early stages of febrile conditions, it stands midway between asthenic activity of Aconite and Belladonna and the asthenic sluggishness and torpidity of

Gelsemium.

3) Nervous, sensitive, anaemic persons with false plethora and easy flushing.

4) Haemorrhages : Bright red blood from any orifice.

5) It corresponds to Grauvogl’s Oxygeniod Constitution.

6) Desire for stimulants.

7) Aversion to meat & milk.

8) Headache better cold applications.

9) Ailments from : 111 effects of sunheat. Exposure to cold.

sections.title: PARTICULARS
sections.content:
Headache

Causation ; Sunheat, Cold. Location : Right sided headache from vertex to supraorbital region.

Sensation : Congestive headache, Throbbing sensation, bruising, pressing or stitching pain & soreness to touch, cold, noise, Jar. gt i

Modalities : Aggravation—Right side, shaking the head, stooping and motion. Amelioration ; Cold application.

Eyes

Acute conjunctivitis. Hyperaemia of Optic disc and retina with blurred vision Eyes inflamed, red

with Gunning sensation, sore and redness looking and retinal congestion. Sensation as if grains of sand were under eyelids.

Ears

First stage of otitis. Membrana tympani red and bulging; Acute otitis, when Belladonna fails. Earache after expo-sure to cold or wet Inflammatery earache with burning or throbbing pain or sharp, stitching pain.

Gastrointestinal Symptoms

Throat: Inflammation of the fauces. Ulcerated throat. Sore throat, dry, red inflamed with much pain—First stage of diphtheria to lessen the fever. Sore throat of singers.

Stomach : Aversian to meat & milk. Desire for stimulants. First stage of gastritis, with pain swelling and tenderness at the pit of the stomach. Vomiting of undigested food, bright red blood. Sour eructations.

Abdomen : First stage of dysentery with much blood in discharges. Stool watery. Contains mucus and blood, urging but no tenesmus. Constipation with prolapse and haemor-rhoids. Haemorrhoids, inflamed or bleeding bright red blood.

Respiratory Symptoms :

Nose : Congested mucous membranes, First stage of all cold in the head, predisposition to catch cold. Catarrhal fever. Epistaxis.; bright red blood.

Chest: First stage of all inflammatory affections. Conges tion of lungs ; cough, hard, dry with sore chest. Short painful tickling cough. Cough better at night. Expectoration of pure blood in

pneumonia, Bronchitis of young children. Haemop-tysis. Urinary Symptoms :

Frequent desire to urinate, urine spurts out with every cough. Haematuria. Incontinence. Irritation at neck of bladder. Polyuria. Diurnal enuresis. Female Genital Symptoms :

Menses every three weeks. Profuse with pressure in abdomen and small of the back and pain on top of the head.

author: Dubey

sections.title: INTRODUCTION
sections.content: Fluoric acid is a colourless liquid obtained by distillation. It unites with water violently and dissolves all ordinary metals. But heavy metals like platinum, gold, silver, mercury, lead, etc. are not soluble in Fluoric acid. It is a strong irritant and causes burns. It is a DEEP and LONG ACTING remedy.

sections.content:
It acts on skin, deep tissue, veins and bones.

Its action on the skin, causes ulcers of syphilitic nature and on the bones its action results in caries and necrosis.. Much weakness and premature old age are also

manifested by Fluoric acid.

sections.title: PARTICULARS
sections.content:
Ulcer

Ulcer of syphilitic or psoric origin are very successfully treated by Fluoric acid. Old cicatrices become red and round edged and threaten to become open ulcers.

Varicose veins and ulcers in obstinate and long standing cases; especially in women who have borne many children, are admirably dealt with by Fluoric acid.

The ulcers have red edges and vesiciles; decubitus, from which copious offensive and acrid discharge comes out, with violent lightning like pain. The pain is confined to a small spot; the Pains are aggravated by warmth and relieved by cold.

All caries and necrosis, especially of long bones whether psoric, or syphilitic or caused by abuse of Mercury or Silica, it matters little, can be satisfactorily tackled by Fluoric acid.

In the case of naevus of children and capillary aneurysm, Fluoric acid can be thought of as an effective remedy to give complete relief.

Furthermore, for the exostosis of long bones or bones of face, rapid caries of teeth, fistula dentalis or lachrymalis. Flouric acid is an infallible remedy.

General Modalities : Aggravation: By warmth. Amelioration: By cold application.

Relations

Complementary to: Silicea and Coca. Followed by: Sulph., Nit. ac. It follows: Sil. as Sil. follows Puls.

sections.title: INTRODUCTION
sections.content:
Gelsemium is said to be the “KING OF POLIO”, by virtue of its being a great paralyser. It is a drug of importance in Homoeopathy not for its great number of symptoms but due to its well marked and clearly characteristic symptoms which are very often met within our day to day practice.

Glonoine—Nitro—glycerine is a combination of two elements—Glycerine, which is a most inert and bland oil used as a constituent of toilet and Nitrogen, which is a colourless, tasteless and odourless gas. When both of them are mixed in 1:4 proportion, potentised and proved according to the doctrine of proving, it becomes one of the most valuable medicines with alarming characters Its SUDDENNESS, BURSTING, SENSATIONS, pains surging upwards which threaten to lift and shatter the cranium are very much striking and characteristic. Dr. Hughes points out in his pharmacodynamics that “though the old school uses Glonoine for various therapeutic purposes the medicine owes its introduction to eonstantine Hering one of the greatest disciples of the Master in the field of Homoeopathy.”

sections.title: CLINICAL
sections.content:
Ataxia, Brain affection, Cerebro spinal meningitis, Cold, Cough, Constipation, Convulsion, Epilepsy, Dengue fever, Diarrhoea, Diphteria, Eye affections, Fevers, Headache, Heart affection, Hysteria, Locomotor Ataxia, Menstrual disorders, Myalgia, Neuralgia, Paralysis, Rheumatism, Sleep disordered, Tremor, Urinary affection, Vertigo, Writer's cramp, etc.

Angina pectoris, Apoplexy, Brain affection, Bnght’s disease, Convulsion, Epilepsy, Headache, Heart affections, Meningitis, Menstrual disorders, Menopausal syndrome, Neuralgia, Rheumatism, Sun-stroke, etc.

sections.title: SPHERES OF ACTION
sections.content:
It acts on brain, spinal cord, occiput, neck, motor nerves, eye lids, vision, mucus membrane, sexual organs and blood. It is a right-sided remedy.

PATHOGENESIS

Acting on the roots of motor cerebral nerve centres, motor area or the spinal cord and both voluntary and involuntary motor nerves, Gels, produces a general state of paresis, mental and physical. This is followed by cutaneous anaesthesia. The mind is sluggish and stupefied; the whole muscular system is relaxed; head and limbs feel heavy; even ptosis and diplopia may occur. Muscles refuse to obey the order of the will. It has functional paralysis of all descriptions. Tremor i. the key-note of this great remedy, and gradually total paralysis may take place, Hence, Gels, is said to be a GREAT PARALYSER.

CONSTITUTION

Look of the patient: It is an acute drug. So consideration of the constiution is not very important. But is usually more suited to children, old people and anaemic girls.

Temperament: Nervous and hysterical temperament. Relation with heat and cold: No definite standard can be set in this respect. Miasm: Psora is in the background,

291

It acts especially on the brain, pneumo-gastric and vaso-motor nerves.

Acting upon the brain, especially medulla oblongata, pneumogastric and peripheral vaso-motor nerves, it produces cerebral hyperaemia, palpitation of heart, severe headache, resembling those resulting from exposure to sun’s rays or sunstroke. It also causes violent and sudden disturbance in circulation with sensation of expansion, bursting and throbbing.

CONSTITUTION

Physical make-up: Especially suited to plethoric sensitive persons who are very irritable and easily excited by slightest opposition.

Temperament: Nervous temperament. Relation with heat and cold: Hot patient.

Miasm: Psora is in the background.

sections.title: PARTICULARS
sections.content:
Headache

Causation: Heat of summer and fright.

Location: Occipital headache, begins on occiput and spreads over the whole head and lastly settles over the forehead andieyes.

Headfiche

Character: From working under gas light, when heat falls on the head or WALKING IN THE SUN, from heat of stove or hair cut during pregnancy and menopause.

Sensation: Head feels ENORMOUSLY LARGE as if the skull were too small for the brain and as if skull were being lifted up.

Character of headache: Severe THROBBING, PULSATING type of headache. The patient holds the head with both hands. There is intense pain. Sensation as if the head would burst; sometimes there is great soreness in the head.

Heaviness of the head with rush of blood towards the head as if all the blood has gone towards the head. SUNSTROKE and SUN HEADACHE—increases and decreases with the sun.

Headache in place of menses.

Modalities: Aggravation from shaking jar, stooping, lying down, SUN'S RAYS and while working under the gas light.

Better by bending head backwards and from covering.

Apoplexy

In threatened apoplexy with cerebral congestion or alternate congestion of the head and heart. The brain feels too large, full, bursting, with rush of blood towards he head, blood seems to be pumped upwards; throbs at every jar. Terrific shock in the head synchronous with the pulse. There is throbbing sensation. The patient holds the head with both hands, cannot lie down, even the pillow seems to beat.

With high blood pressure, there is violent palpitation. Throbbing in carotids, heart's action is slow. In apoplexy when violent pressure keeps on and congestion, continues, If it is given, it will relieve the pressure provided the symptoms agree.

Meningitis

Causation: During the time of dentition.

sections.content:

. Symptoms are WORSE IN THE SUN or exposure to sun’s rays. Sensation of pulsation throughout the body. Surging of blood to head and heart.

Bad effects of mental excitement, fright, fear, mechanical injuries hair cut and SUN STROKE.

6. General weakness and depression from heat of sun or summer 7. Weakness and trembling of tongue, hands, legs and the entire body. 8. Ailments from : Sun, heat of fire, fear, fright, injury and hair-cut.

sections.title: INTRODUCTION
sections.content: Graphites is one of the top ranking ‘WOMEN’S REMEDIES’. It is a deep acting constitutional polychrest drug sony from the mineral kingdom. Ordinarily, the’ crude lead possesses no curative power, but after undergoing the process of potentisation, it earns a respectable place amongst the important medicines in the box of a Homoeopath.

sections.title: CLINICAL
sections.content: Anaemia, Acne, Breast affection, Cancer, Catarrh, Chlorosis, Colic, Constipation, Dropsy, Eresipelas, Eye affection, Ear affection, Gastralgia, Haemorrhoids, Headache, Leucorrhoea, Liver affection, Menopausal syndrome, Menstrual disorders, Stomach and abdominal disorders, Skin affections, Tumours, Urinary disorders, Whooping cough, etc.

sections.title: SPHERES OF ACTION
sections.content:
The chief spheres of action of Graphites are centred upon skin, gastrointestinal tract, sexual organs, glands, etc.

PATHOGENESIS

Its action on skin produces degenerative changes, manifestation of various kinds of skin eruptions from which oozes a WATERY, TRANSPARENT AND STICKY FLUID. It exerts a general influence on nutrition of skin; whereby it causes diarrhoea, chr chronic constipation ete. in the digestive system and excessive menstrual ailment, leucorrhoea, ete. in sexual organs.

CONSTITUTION

Make-up of the body; Usually a lady of climacteric age, fair, fat and flabby, having irregular deposition of fat at selected locations of the body, waxy and anaemic face, split hair, unhealthy skin, brittle and deformed nails, suffering from habitual constipation and with a history of delayed rnenstruation,

Temperament: Irritable and melancholic.

Relation with heat and cold; Very chilly patient.

sections.title: PARTICULARS
sections.content:
Headache

Causation: From grief, vexation, extremes of heat and cold.

Location: Congestive pain especially in the occiput; extends to the nape of neck, stitching pain in temples.

Character of headache: Pain as though the head were numb, violent headache as if the Head would burst, congestive, constriqtive and stitching pain.

Modality: Aggravation at night and during menstruation and relieved by lying down,

author: Dubey
chapter: Dubey Text Book of Materia Medica

sections.title: INTRODUCTION
sections.content: No remedy has wider spheres of usefulness in ease of haemorrhage and disordered blood-vessels than Hamamelis virginica. It also has a decided relation to the effects of mechanical injuries including burns of the first degree. As a local application it ranks with Arnica and Calendula. It is widely said to be the “ACONITE OF THE VENOUS CAPILLARY SYSTEM”. When there is oozing out of venous blood from any where in the body, either from piles or varicose veins or from nose, bowels, uterus, lungs, open injury, ete, the great anti-haemorrhagic homoeopathic medicine that we can think of first, is Hamamelis.

sections.title: CLINICAL
sections.content: Bone affection, Bruises, Bums, Cancer, Consumption, Enteric fever, Eye affection, Gastric Ulcer, Haematemesis, Haematuria, Haemorrhage, Haemorrhoids, Injury, Leucorrhoea, Menstrual disorders. Epistaxis, Rheumatism, Scurvy, Testicles inflammation, Threatened abortion, Ulcers, Varicose veins, etc.

sections.title: SPHERES OF ACTION
sections.content:
It acts on VEINS, CAPILLARIES, liver, portal system, rectum and generative organs.

PATHOGENESIS

Acting upon the coats of veins, it causes relaxation with consequent engorgement and even structural lesions and thereby produce PASSIVE VENOUS HAEMORRHAGE FROM ANY PART.

CONSTITUTION

There is no particular constitution but Ham. is suitable for those who are having HAEMORRHAGIC DIATHESIS and suffer from diseases like PHLEBITIES, VARICOSIS. HAEMORRHOIDS and VENOUS HAEMORRHAGE.

sections.title: GUIDING SYMPTOMS
sections.content:
1. Intense soreness of affected parts is the key-note of this remedy,

2. Bleeding from any orifice or from open wound; blood being DARK PASSIVE AND NON-COAGULABLE.

—_—s

sections.title: PARTICULARS
sections.content:
Haemorrhage

It is better adapted to PASSIVE VENOUS HAEMORRHAGE from any orifice of the body; nose (RHINORRHAGIA, lungs, (HAEMOPTYSIS), stomach (HAEMATEMESIS), bowels (MALAENA), bladder (HAEMATURIA), uterus (MENORRHAGIA), etc.

The character of blood is PROFUSE, DARK, GRUMOUS. Haemorrhage after a fall or rough riding. There is intense somess of the affected parts. Vicarious menstruation is also found in it.

Nose-bleed :

Causation: \diopathic, traumatic, vicarious, of childhood.

Flow is passive, long lasting and venous.

Blood is non-coagulable (Crot.) profuse, which relieves headache.

Eye

It hastens absorption of intraocular haemorrhage.

Haemoptysis

Ticking cough with taste of blood or sulphur; without effort or coughing; sometimes lasts for months or years. Chest feels sore and constricted.

Modality: Aggravation from motion and little exertion.

Haematemesis

Throbbing pain in stomach. PROFUSE BLEEDING DARK BLOOD, SORENESS IN THE

ABDOMEN, haemorrhage from intestine during typhoid or in dysentery, profuse bleeding, dark blood. Anus feels raw and sore. Haemorrhage does not cause any mental anxiety.

Modality: Aaggravation from motion and little exertion.

Haematuria

Dark blood with increased desire to urinate.

Varicosity of veins

May be in the oesophagus (Oesophageal varices), rectum (piles), abdomen, legs, pampiniform plexus of veins of scrotum, etc. Veins dilate, elongate and become tortuous and bleed easily. Blood is dark; ulceration of the varicose veins (Fluoric acid).

full:
INTRODUCTION: No remedy has wider spheres of usefulness in ease of haemorrhage and disordered blood-vessels than Hamamelis virginica. It also has a decided relation to the effects of mechanical injuries including burns of the first degree. As a local application it ranks with Arnica and Calendula. It is widely said to be the “ACONITE OF THE VENOUS CAPILLARY SYSTEM”. When there is oozing out of venous blood from any where in the body, either from piles or varicose veins or from nose, bowels, uterus, lungs, open injury, ete, the great anti-haemorrhagic homoeopathic medicine that we can think of first, is Hamamelis.
CLINICAL: Bone affection, Bruises, Bums, Cancer, Consumption, Enteric fever, Eye affection, Gastric Ulcer, Haematemesis, Haematuria, Haemorrhage, Haemorrhoids, Injury, Leucorrhoea, Menstrual disorders. Epistaxis, Rheumatism, Scurvy, Testicles inflammation, Threatened abortion, Ulcers, Varicose veins, etc.
SPHERES OF ACTION: It acts on VEINS, CAPILLARIES, liver, portal system, rectum and generative organs.

PATHOGENESIS

Acting upon the coats of veins, it causes relaxation with consequent engorgement and even structural lesions and thereby produce PASSIVE VENOUS HAEMORRHAGE FROM ANY PART.

CONSTITUTION

There is no particular constitution but Ham. is suitable for those who are having HAEMORRHAGIC DIATHESIS and suffer from diseases like PHLEBITIES, VARICOSIS. HAEMORRHOIDS and VENOUS HAEMORRHAGE.
GUIDING SYMPTOMS: 1. Intense soreness of affected parts is the key-note of this remedy,

2. Bleeding from any orifice or from open wound; blood being DARK PASSIVE AND NON-COAGULABLE.

—_—s
PARTICULARS: Haemorrhage

It is better adapted to PASSIVE VENOUS HAEMORRHAGE from any orifice of the body; nose (RHINORRHAGIA, lungs, (HAEMOPTYSIS), stomach (HAEMATEMESIS), bowels (MALAENA), bladder (HAEMATURIA), uterus (MENORRHAGIA), etc.

The character of blood is PROFUSE, DARK, GRUMOUS. Haemorrhage after a fall or rough riding. There is intense somess of the affected parts. Vicarious menstruation is also found in it.

Nose-bleed :

Causation: \diopathic, traumatic, vicarious, of childhood.

Flow is passive, long lasting and venous.

Blood is non-coagulable (Crot.) profuse, which relieves headache.

Eye

It hastens absorption of intraocular haemorrhage.

Haemoptysis

Ticking cough with taste of blood or sulphur; without effort or coughing; sometimes lasts for months or years. Chest feels sore and constricted.

Modality: Aggravation from motion and little exertion.
