name: Veratrum Album
author: Dubey
chapter: Dubey Text Book of Materia Medica

sections.title: INTRODUCTION
sections.content:
White Hellebore, as it is commonly called, was known for centuries as one of the great remedies for collaspe and pain. Hahnemann’s provings established this fact by testing its reaction on the healthy provers. He tells.us in his Materia Medica Pura some revealing things about this drug, particularly about its mental sphere which are as follows -

“Physicians have no notion of the power possessed by this drug to promote a cure of almost one-third of the insane in lunatic asylums because they know not the pecular kind of insanity in which to employ it, nor the dose in which it should be administered in order to be efficacious and yet not injurious.

sections.title: CLINICAL
sections.content: Angina pectoris, Apoplexy, Asthma, Cholera, Colic, Collaspe, Constipation, Cramps, Debility, Diarrhoea, Epilepsy, Gastric and abdominal disorders, Headache, Influenza, Intermittent fever, Labour, Mania, Melancholia, Meningitis, Menstrual disorders, Rheumatism, Vertigo, etc.

sections.title: SPHERES OF ACTION
sections.content:
Veratrum album acts especially upon the system of nutrition affecting profoundly the vegetative sphere. It also acts upon the blood and nervous system.

PATHOGENESIS

It causes disorganisation of blood and seperates it into its constitutent components. The circulation becomes embarassed and as a result, there is general torpor of the vegetative system. It gives rise to choleric condition, general coldness, prostration, collaspe, copious watery vomiting and purging, spasmodic colic, cramps and spasms. Its action on the nervous system results in excitation of the cerebral nerves producing thereby delirum and mania, in addition to great exhaustion of nerve power.

CONSTITUTION

As it is mainly an acute remedy, no importane is to be attached to be physical make- up or constitution as such of the patient. But it is especially suited to the complaints of People too young and too old (i.e. extremes of age)

ee ———

sections.title: PARTICULARS
sections.content:
Gastro-intestinal symptoms

The usual complaints met with in this drug, relating to the gastrointestinal tract, are VIOLENT DIARRHOEA AND VOMITING OR CONSTIPATION. Violence in everything is the striking peculiarity of this remedy.

Stomach : There is cold feeling injthe stomach with cutting pain as if from knives. There is also sinking feeling in the stomach. Nausea and vomiting just after eating and drinking, are frequently found The patient craves acid and refreshing juicy things.

There is great thirst for huge.quanitity of icy cold-water,

Constipation

* Sensation: Desire is felt in epigastrium (Ign. —in rectum Nux vorn.).

* Character of stool: Dry, hard, in round black balls, very much gainful with much straining until the patient is exhausted.

Diarrhoea

¢ Causation: From fright, eating, drinking and taking fruits. * Sensation; Cutting pain in abdomen as from knives. * Character of stool: Stool is PROFUSE, watery, gushing and mixed with flakes.

¢ During stools: There is colic with cramps commencing in hands and feet spreading all over the body, with COLD SWEAT ON FOREHEAD.

e After stool: There is great prostration.

* Modality: Aggravation from fright, Jeast motion, eating and drinking.

* Concomitants: Diarrhoea before and during menses (Bov., Ammon. Carb.).

Cholera

¢ Causation: From fright or taking impure drinks.

¢ During cholera: There is PROFUSENESS OF DISCHARGES which runs through the whole remedy e.g. PROFUSE PURGING, VOMITING, SWEAT, etc.

Violent vomiting with profuse diarrhoea, excessive vomiting and purging. There is profuse, rice-watery stool which gushes out.

, a *

name: Veratrum Viride
author: Dubey
chapter: Dubey Text Book of Materia Medica

sections.title: INTRODUCTION
sections.content:
Veratrum viride is a small but powerful drug. It is mostly used in severe acute cases, such as severe form of headache, sunstroke, basilar meningitis, convulsion, acute rheumatism, etc. It has direct action over heart, causing depression of heartbeat and low pulse rate. So never misuse it and never repeat it very frequently just to control the heart’s action or bring down the pulse. Like any other remedy it can only be given for the totality of symptoms.

Hale was chifly instrumental in introducing Veratrum viride into Homoeopathy, using it particularly in pneumonia.

Belladonna has got muchsimilarity with Veratrum viride. So, never substitute it when Veratrum viride is indicated. Individual and comparative study of these two drugs are necessary for a correct prescription.

sections.title: CLINICAL
sections.content: Apoplexy, Asthma, Brain affection, Chorea, Convulsion, Erysipelas, Headache, Heart affection, Hyperpyrexia, Fever, Meningitis, Pneumonia, Rheumatism, Sunstroke, etc.

sections.title: SPHERES OF ACTION
sections.content:
Veraturm viride acts on heart, blood vessels, pneumo-gastric nerve, lungs and joints. It particularly acts on the cervical portion of spinal cord and the base of the brain.

Acting on the heart, it lowers both systolic and diastolic blood pressure. It also on the internal organs such as the base of brain, chest, spine, stomach, etc. and produces congestion.

CONSTITUTION

Since Veratrum viride is mostly an acute drug, consideration of constitution is not of much importance. The patient is however, full blooded, plethoric, with bloated and livid face.

1.A narrow, well developed red streak right through the middle of the toungue, is the red-strand symptom of this drug.

sections.title: PARTICULARS
sections.content:
Meningitis

Causation: Meningitis may be caused by exposure to heat. Onset: Sudden and violent.

Character: Basiter meningitis; convulsion, dim vision, RETRACTED, PUPILS DILATED, tetanic convulsion, cold and clammy perspiration. Pain in the nape of neck, cannot hold the head up; opisthotonos.

* Aggravation: By motion, raising the head, exposure to heat and cold and sitting erect. ¢ Amelioration: By remaining quiet, lying down and rubbing.

Apoplexy

Congestive apoplexy, head hot; blood-shot eyes, thick speech, pulse full and hard as iron. Bloated livid face. Hippocratic face, with red streak down the middle of the tongue.

Sunstroke

Face is flushed; head full; throbbing of arteries, bearing of pulse throughout the body; vertigo with nausea, Convulsive twitching of the faeial muscles. Sensitive to sound; double vision or partial vision (Glon., Gels).

Headache

Causation: Exposure to sun's rays, heat and extreme cold, suppression of menses and lochia. Onset: Sudden and violent Onset. Character: Violent nerypus sick headache: Congestion from suppressed menses. Intense, almost apopletic headache; throbbini of arteries; head hot and face flushed.

Modalities

* Aggravation: By motion, raising the head, warmth, * Amelioration: By remaining quiet, lying down and tight bandaging. Concomitants: Nausea and vomiting, with blood-shot eyes.

CLINICAL: Apoplexy, Asthma, Brain affection, Chorea, Convulsion, Erysipelas, Headache, Heart affection, Hyperpyrexia, Fever, Meningitis, Pneumonia, Rheumatism, Sunstroke, etc.
SPHERES OF ACTION: Veraturm viride acts on heart, blood vessels, pneumo-gastric nerve, lungs and joints. It particularly acts on the cervical portion of spinal cord and the base of the brain.

Acting on the heart, it lowers both systolic and diastolic blood pressure. It also on the internal organs such as the base of brain, chest, spine, stomach, etc. and produces congestion.

CONSTITUTION

Since Veratrum viride is mostly an acute drug, consideration of constitution is not of much importance. The patient is however, full blooded, plethoric, with bloated and livid face.

1.A narrow, well developed red streak right through the middle of the toungue, is the red-strand symptom of this drug.
PARTICULARS: Meningitis

Causation: Meningitis may be caused by exposure to heat. Onset: Sudden and violent.

Character: Basiter meningitis; convulsion, dim vision, RETRACTED, PUPILS DILATED, tetanic convulsion, cold and clammy perspiration. Pain in the nape of neck, cannot hold the head up; opisthotonos.

* Aggravation: By motion, raising the head, exposure to heat and cold and sitting erect. ¢ Amelioration: By remaining quiet, lying down and rubbing.

Apoplexy

Congestive apoplexy, head hot; blood-shot eyes, thick speech, pulse full and hard as iron. Bloated livid face. Hippocratic face, with red streak down the middle of the tongue.

Sunstroke

Face is flushed; head full; throbbing of arteries, bearing of pulse throughout the body; vertigo with nausea, Convulsive twitching of the faeial muscles. Sensitive to sound; double vision or partial vision (Glon., Gels).

Headache

Causation: Exposure to sun's rays, heat and extreme cold, suppression of menses and lochia. Onset: Sudden and violent Onset. Character: Violent nerypus sick headache: Congestion from suppressed menses. Intense, almost apopletic headache; throbbini of arteries; head hot and face flushed.

Modalities

* Aggravation: By motion, raising the head, warmth, * Amelioration: By remaining quiet, lying down and tight bandaging. Concomitants: Nausea and vomiting, with blood-shot eyes.

name: Viburnum Opulus
author: Dubey
chapter: Dubey Text Book of Materia Medica

sections.title: INTRODUCTION
sections.content: This plant is a native of Great Britain. It bears red berries which are sour and are utilised in making jelly. One learns most about this medicine from Male’s Materia Medica of the New Remedies. It is a great remedy for women’s complaints.

sections.title: CLINICAL
sections.content: After-pains, Cramps. Dysmenorrhoea- spasmodic, membranous, neuralgic, Labour pains,— false, Miscarriage.

sections.title: SPHERES OF ACTION
sections.content:
Viburnum acts especially upon the female genital organs uterus, ovaries and other genital organs. Left side is more affected than the right.

CONSTITUTION Suited to tall, slender, dark or fair haired hys-terical subjects.

1) This remedy is valuable in spasmodic and membranous dysmemorrhoea with

following indications

Menses Time too late

Duration Lasting a few hours.

Quantity Scanty

Character of blood Thin light coloured and offensive in odour.

Before menses Severe bearing down pains, pain in anterior muscles

of thigh, Heavy aching feeling in sacral and pubic regions.

Character of blood : Blood clotted, bright red. There is also oozing of dark blood, highly coagulated, forming occasion-ally long, black, stringy clots. Flow profuse and did not cease entirely until next period.

Vicarious menstruation from lungs and bowels. Menor-rhagia at climaxis; active & Constant flowing with frequent clots.

name: Vinca Minor
author: Dubey
chapter: Dubey Text Book of Materia Medica

sections.title: INTRODUCTION
sections.content:
This remedy was proved by Rosenburg on four healthy persons who took the tincture in 20—60 drops doses. The most important field of its action is located on skin, hair & female genital organs. It has been successfully used in eczema, plica polonica, alopecia & crusta lactea and to con-trol the uterine haemorrhages.

On the head, there is numerous humid eruptions which itch burn intensely; from these a moisture oozes that mats the hairs together. Corrosive itching of scalp with irrestible desire to scratch. The skin of the body is highly sensitive with redness and soreness from slight rubbing

Another use of this remedy is to control uterine haemor-rhage. There is excessive menstruation with great weakness. It also controls haemorrhages either from fibroids or climaxis Haemorrhages are usually passive in character.

name: Vipera
author: Dubey
chapter: Dubey Text Book of Materia Medica

sections.title: INTRODUCTION
sections.content:
Vipera affects the blood and blood vessels, leading to haemorrhages & inflammation of the vessels themselves. Viper poisoning causes a temporary paraplegia of the. lower extremities extending upwards. It is indicated in phlebitis, lymphangioma, varicose veins, enlargement of liver, polyneuritis & polio—myelitis etc.

The characteristic indication of this remedy is varicose veins & acute phlebitis is “bursting sensation in affected limbs & unbearable pain when limbs are allowed to hang down”. Patient is obliged to keep the extemities elevated. Veins are swollen, sensitive & painful with bursting sensation.

The next important use of this remedy is in enlargement of liver when there is violent pain in the enlarged liver in jaundice & fever. Pain radiates to shoulder & hip.

name: Xanthoxylum
author: Dubey
chapter: Dubey Text Book of Materia Medica

sections.title: INTRODUCTION
sections.content: INTRODUCTION : Just like Sepia, this remedy is particularly a woman’s remedy, specially for the nervous women.

sections.title: CLINICAL
sections.content:
After pains. Headache. Hemiplegia. Indigestion. Neuralgia-crural. Neuralgic dysmenorrhoea. Sciatica. Toothache. Uterine fibroma.

SPHERE OF ACTION AND PATHOGENESIS

Its specific action is on nervous system and mucous membrane, causing excessive mucous secretion of the mouth by stimulating secretion from all glands with ducts opening in the mouth. & female genital system.

CONSTITUTION

Best adapted to persons who are thin, emaciated and nervous with nervous temperament having Psoric and Syphilitic miasm’s in the back ground.

sections.title: GUIDING SYMPTOMS
sections.content:
1) This remedy is infallible for neuralgic dysmenorrhoea in women of nervous, delicate nature—who give history of too early, usually thick blackish stringy-blood, menstrual flow intermitting every other day and generally lasting for 2 weeks. The most important is the agonizing pain along the course of the genito crural nerve. The pain shoots down as low as knee and no position really relieves. Generally associated with backache and headache. During pain patient desires to take deep breath. Dysmenorrhoea may be attended with left sided ovarian neuralgia. (Lil Tig, Lachesis, Medo, Thuja)

2) Leucorrhoea in place of menses (Cocculus., lodum., Nux-Mos., Phos.)

3) Headache : Specially when caused by suppression of menses. During headache there is sensation as if head were surrounded by tight band (Gels-., Nitric Acid., Carbo. Acid., Sulph.) Head feels full. Occipital headache. Usu-ally headache is associated with sleepiness, flatulence, ringing in ears.

Modalities : Aggravation—In the morning. Amelioration : By cold water, in open air.

name: X-Ray
author: Dubey
chapter: Dubey Text Book of Materia Medica

sections.title: INTRODUCTION
sections.content:
It is one of the most neglected drugs of |Biniw

a }

Materia Medica. No, doubt it was proved long ago, moite than ninety years back but it is rarely used by us, Homoeopaths. If we analyse the symptoms of potentised X-Ray, we can easily know the depth and wide, range of action of this medicine. In various kinds of complicated miasmatic diseases, sycotic, syphylitic, psoric even mixed miasmatic diseases, if we use this medicine at proper time, we may help in curing various kinds of clinical dreaded conditions such as obstinate eczema, psoriasis, vitelego, alopecia, corn, various kinds of warts, neurofibroma, various kinds of ulcers, and wounds which refuse to heal, fistula, caries and necrosis of bones, obstinate cases of rheumatism, arthritis and gouts, paresis and paralysis, retarded growth, diabetis melitus, and anaemia. Its homoeopathic action is centrifugal towards the periphery. It is a very deep acting, long lasting medicine and should not be repeated off and on.

GUIDING SYMPTOMS :

1) History of repeated exposure to X-Ray, either for diagnostic or therapeutic purpose and/or history of Radium Therapy. There may be or may not be such history. If symptoms agree, X-Ray should be thought of.

2) When well indicated medicines fail to relieve or cure the mixed miasmatic conditions, it should be thought of.

3) Long lasting suppression of miasmatic conditions—it brings out to the surface suppressed symptoms such as gonorrheal discharge, syphilitic chancers, skin eruptions etc.

4) It covers mixed miasmatic states such as psora, sychosis & syphilis, when the constitutional medicines are not indicated or are failing to do much good to the patient.

5) If there is much organic changes leading to a stage of incurability, then in such

cases when individualistic symptoms are very few and more disease symptoms appear, X-Ray may turn the case into curable state.

name: Zincum Metallicum
author: Dubey
chapter: Dubey Text Book of Materia Medica

sections.title: INTRODUCTION
sections.content:
Last but not the least, here comes Zincum metallicum which is a great remedy for the affection of nerves. Burt says, “WHAT IRON IS TO BLOOD, ZINC IS TO NERVE”. All the metals and minerals are of great therapeutic value to human beings, although all of them have not yet been proved. Amongst these, Zinc is one having great curative power which has been already established. This is one of the remedies quite often looked for by a true Homoeopath.

The relief of human suffering is a noble cause. Those who devote their life in this cause truly deserves the gratitude of their fellows. In the history of the healing art, one such name is Wilhelm Heinrich Schuessler, one of the outstanding intellects of the ninentinth century and a man whose scientific vision was far ahead of his time. Dr. Schuessler was not only a doctor of medicine, but he was also a physiological chemist and a physicist. His keen, analytical mind was able to assimilate and to co-ordinate the far- reaching physiological discoveries of great contemporary scientists. As a practising physician, he was able to put his carefully worked-out theories to the test and the brilliant results he achieved led to the formulation of his unique system of cellular therapeutics, to which he gave the name - Biochemistry/Biochemic System of Medicne. Thus Dr. Wilhelm Heinrich Schuessler is considered as the founder of the Biochemic System of Medicine.

DR. WILHELM HEINRICH SCHUESSLER

Dr. Wilhelm Heinrich Schuessler was born on the 2ist of August 1821 in Oldenburg, Germany. Since childhood, Schuessler was a studious boy and had remarkable capabilities. He devoted most of his time learning foreign languages like Latin, Greek, Spanish, French, English and Italian. He wanted to become a Homeopathic physician when he grew up, but his brother told him that he would assist him to become one, only if he became a legally qualified practitioner. Keeping to his word, Schuessler studied medicine at the University of Berlin, Paris, Geissen and Prague. He then qualified as a homeopathic practitioner and started his practice at Oldenburg.

Died : 30th March, 1898 Dr. Schuessler was very much influenced by Rudolph Virchow (the founder of cellular pathology), who taught that all diseases are based on a change in the function of cells in the body. Another important person who influenced him greatly was Professor Moleschott, who pointed out that the structure and vitality of the organs depends upon the presence of inorganic constituents, Based on the theories of these two, Schuessler formulated his own doctrine, which he called the Cell salt therapy or the Biochemic system of medicine. He is also referred as the Father of deficiency therapy.

Dr Schuessler believed that when a human being is reduced to ashes by heat, there are only twelve minerals left. These he called as the tissue salts. They are responsible for the natural balance and vitality of the body, According to him, deficiency of any of these tissue salts produces a diseased condition in the human organism, and replenishment or supplementation of the body by the deficient salt, in physiological doses restores health in the organism. Schuessler potentised these tissue salts and made them into biochemic remedies.

Born : 21st August, 1821

sections.title: CLINICAL
sections.content: Abdominal and gastric disorders, Alcoholism, Asthma, Brain-fag, Brain affection, Chilblains Convulsion, Constipation, Dentition, Diarrhoea, Debility, Eye affection Eruptions suppressed, Fidgety, Gastralgia, Headache, Memory weak, Meningitis, Neuralgia, Urinary affection, etc.

sections.title: SPHERES OF ACTION
sections.content:
Zincum met., finds its main seat of action on cerebro-spinal system, blood, digestive system and kidneys.

Zincum met., acts on the cerebro-spinal nervous system producing a picture of cerebral depression. “FAG”, brain-fag and nerve-fag; a condition of erythism in brain, medulla oblongata arid spinal cord. Its action on blood causes anaemia and lessens the number of RBC. Acting on the digestive system, it sets in an abnormal appetite with constipation or diarrhoea. Under its influence, kidneys exhibit congestion and defective absorption of threshold substances.

sections.title: GUIDING SYMPTOMS
sections.content:
1. Cerebral depression; nervous exhaustion and defeocting, vitality run through the whole drug.

2. Brain and nerve power wanting. The patient is too WEAK to develop exanthemata, to expectorate, to urinate, to understand, to, memorise, to menstruate, and the like.

3. There is INCESSANT AND VIOLENT FIDGETY FEELING IN FEET AND LOWER EXTREMITIES; MUST MOVE THEM CONSTANTLY.

sections.title: PARTICULARS
sections.content:
Head

Vertigo; falling to the left when walking. Sensation of eyes drawing together, followed by nausea. vomiting and trembling. Heaviness and dullness in head; hemicrania. Automatic motion of head and hands. Forehead is cool and base of brain hot.

Headache from wine or alcohol, after taking even a small quantity. In hydrocephalus and meningitis. the patient rolls the head from side to side. Bores the head into the pillow. Impending paralysis of brain. There are symptoms of effusion into ventricles.

Extremities

Due to defective vitality and lack of brain and nerve power, there is INCESSANT AND VIOLENT

FIDGETY FEELING AND WEAKNESS IN THE FEET AND, THEREFORE, THE PATIENT WANTS TO .KEEP “THEM MOVING CONSTANTLY.

There is also excessive nervous movement of feet in bed for hours after retiring, even when asleep. Feet are sweaty and sore about the toes; foetid and suppressed foot sweat. There is great weakness and trembling of extremities. During sweat, the patient cannot tolerate covering, Sweat relieves. There is general amelioration by menstrual flow.

Convulsion

Causation: Cerebral affection; paralysis of brain, effusion into ventricles, during dentition period in children, from suppression of eruption and fright.

The patient cries out during sleep; whole body jerks while sleeping. The patient wakes up frightened; rolls the head from side to side; bores the head into the plllow; face alternately pale and red; PALE FACE,
